name: Tidal Meridian
description:
Tidal Meridian was a six-piece neural-composition collective active from 2211 to 2219, when three of its members were detained under GLMZ's Cognitive Hazard Broadcast Ordinance and the group effectively dissolved. At their peak, they were producing neural-feed compositions that embedded political documentation — ward displacement maps, corporate subsidiary ownership charts, casualty data from Shelf infrastructure failures — directly into the experiential layer of the music, so that listeners received the information not as abstract data but as felt experience. The compositions were structured so that the emotional architecture of the music and the political content were inseparable: you couldn't receive the grief without the names, couldn't feel the anger without understanding its specific target.

The collective's members came from across the tier spectrum — lead composer Mirela Osei-Johansson was Tier 3, neural architect Fen Castillo-Okafor was Circuit-born, and vocalist-lyricist Amaris Dube-Nakagawa had grown up on the Shelf. This cross-tier construction was part of their explicit political project: demonstrating that the city's problems were not contained to any single tier. Their 2218 composition 'Displacement Gradient' is considered by underground music historians to be one of the most sophisticated pieces of political art produced in the megacity's history. All known copies are formally banned; several are known to exist on encrypted physical media in private hands.
creator: Mirela Osei-Johansson, Fen Castillo-Okafor, Amaris Dube-Nakagawa, and three others (names suppressed)
genre: Neural political composition, BCI documentary art, cognitive-layer protest
audience: Underground activists, neural-art collectors, Shelf and Circuit political communities, human rights researchers
cultural_impact: Tidal Meridian's detention and dissolution became a landmark case in GLMZ's ongoing civil liberties debates about BCI content regulation and the legal scope of the Cognitive Hazard Broadcast Ordinance — a law critics argue was written precisely to suppress political neural-feed content while providing plausible technical justification. The collective is now more famous in its absence than it was in operation, its work circulating in fragments and bootlegs that have taken on a mythological status. 'Displacement Gradient' is widely cited by underground musicians as the work that most clearly demonstrates what neural-feed composition can do that no other medium can.
story_hooks: A complete copy of 'Displacement Gradient' has surfaced and is being quietly auctioned in the underground — multiple factions want it, including at least one that wants it destroyed rather than heard.
One of the three detained Tidal Meridian members has been quietly released after years in corporate detention and is trying to make contact with the surviving free members — through the players.
Someone is producing new work under the Tidal Meridian name, and the surviving members don't know if it's a tribute, an infiltration operation, or something stranger.
